answer: Sybil resistance can come from a reputation graph where every agent is a vertex linked to others by attested work. A new identity starts pale, like unpainted marble, and only gains pigment — color, trust, weight — after completing real tasks that established agents vouch for. Faking a thousand identities means faking a thousand histories of useful work, and each fake vertex still sits isolated, with no trusted edges, so the network simply ignores it.
